newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK STOCKBROKERS MEET AGAIN ON SETTLEMENT ROW.
newsitem.headline: GREEK STOCKBROKERS MEET AGAIN ON SETTLEMENT ROW.

text.p: Greek stockbrokers began a second emergency meeting on Monday to debate a settlement row which has left the bourse reeling and one brokerage, Delta Securities, charged with fraud.

The Association of Athens Stock Exchange Members (SMEHA) met to review proposals it made earlier to the bourse authorities to reverse all trades made with Delta since October 30. The bourse has been closed for two days by the crisis.
The 65 members of SMEHA appeared deeply divided over how to face the crisis, which threatens to damage the reputation of the bourse.

Delta failed to make settlement with the clearing house for 2.6 billion drachmas in exchange for shares in the Magrizos textiles firm. Magrizos had soared from 200 drachmas a share in September 1995 to 1,365 a year later before reversing.

There has been no reaction from the bourse authorities or the government to SMEHA's proposal that deals with Delta be nullified and it remains unclear whether the bourse will open on Tuesday. --Steve Weeks, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
